utterances.text: Yet you told the investigators of the OTP, "I have no connection to the detainees in the KP Dom, nor did I ever propose to anyone -- nor did I ever propose that anyone be released from KP Dom." You remember making that statement?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying now as well that I had nothing to do with them, and that I never had anyone to make proposals to in respect of somebody's release from the KP Dom, and I never gave such a proposal to anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you did pass along the requests, in one case to the Crisis Staff and in another case to the Foca Tactical Group, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, that's different, passing on a piece of paper, passing on somebody's request. But I did not have any agreement with the person who was sending the request or with the addressee; but to pass on a paper, yes, the truth is that that did happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to show you, with the assistance of the usher, Exhibit D67. This is your signature, right, as acting warden?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is my signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you have written a short note to the Crisis Staff saying, "Please find enclosed the request which we are forwarding to you for further action," right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You received the request from Enes Zekovic while you were the acting warden in the KP Dom, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As long as it's written here, that's the way it is, but ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was it that you came to receive this request from Enes Zekovic? How did it end up in your hands?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date is the 15th of May and it says here quite properly that his request is being forwarded, his request to be released from detention, but now I would like to see what it says on the actual request, who it was sent to. If it was sent to the Crisis Staff, then I sent this document directly to them, because I sent the document, forwarded it, to the same addressee that this person had put. How it reached me, I really don't know. On the 15th of May, probably somebody brought it to me, either through some of the guards that they knew. Perhaps they asked one of the guards, "Please hand this over to Milorad." But then I passed this on immediately. I don't know what it says on the request itself, who it was addressed to, but as long as the address that I put was to the Crisis Staff of the Serbian municipality, then probably that is what the request actually said. Is this only this paper, without the actual contents, the actual request? Or do we have the request as well?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, I'd like to show you Exhibit D67/1 and that is the text of the request. We can see from D67/1 that this request, signed by Enes Zekovic, was addressed to the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Enes Zekovic also addressed this to the Crisis Staff of the Serbian Municipality of Foca, and through my own letter, I forwarded this very same request to the Crisis Staff, because there was no point -- I mean, he must have known this for sure because he addressed it to the Crisis Staff itself. He also realised it was no use sending this to Milorad. Maybe he trusted me, that I would forward this, that I would pass it on and that it would actually get into the hands of the person or people he addressed it to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Krnojelac, this letter wasn't addressed to you at all, was it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not addressed to me. It says here the Crisis Staff, to the Crisis Staff of the Serbian Municipality of Foca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yet you prepared a note forwarding this letter on behalf of the KP Dom to the Crisis Staff, right? You didn't just pass this letter on to the Crisis Staff, because it wasn't addressed to you.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I forwarded it to those to whom it was addressed. I personally think that Mr. Zekovic knew that I had nothing to do with them. If you allow me to say this, if this was a convicted person who was serving his prison sentence, then I would have forwarded that to the ministry. However, here it says "to the Crisis Staff of the Serbian Municipality of Foca." I passed it on to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. With the assistance of the usher --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you, too. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- I would like the witness shown Exhibit D66. This is again a note signed by you in your official capacity as the warden. This one is addressed to the Foca Tactical Group, dated 30th July 1992, and this also is a cover sheet forwarding two requests for release from detainees. Here you've called them prisoners of war, but really they were being detained at the KP Dom, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here, "Please find enclosed requests for release from detention of prisoners of war Ismet Pasovic and Sadik --" I can't see; these glasses aren't good. I can't read the last name -- "for further procedure." I don't know who it is addressed to, but yes, this is my signature, and I forwarded this document as well to the Tactical Group. It probably pertained to the Tactical Group, this request did, I mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, I'd like to have you shown Exhibit D66/1. This is a copy of one of the requests that you attached, right, that you forwarded on to the Foca Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, here it says, "To the KP Dom warden, request for release from the KP Dom." That's the subject. Please, there is no need for me to repeat this: Part of the KP Dom was rented out to the military.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you're right, there is no need for you to repeat that. My question to you is, this was addressed to you as the warden, right? Not to the Tactical Group.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the warden of the KP Dom. I have to give an explanation, if at all possible, please. I was not their warden. I sent it to the Tactical Group because their warden was in the Tactical Group. So that's why I forwarded the document to the Tactical Group, because I had no authority whatsoever over these persons --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- who were brought into custody.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to make one thing absolutely clear. Are you now saying that you were not the warden of the KP Dom, even after the 17th of July, 1992? You've given us an explanation of what you said your duties were, but I just want to be clear about the title. Are you denying now that you had the title of warden of KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Warden of the KP Dom and the manager of the Drina Economic Unit, both.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this letter was, in fact, addressed to you, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, a part of the KP Dom was let out to the army, and their warden was in the Tactical Group. I was not their warden.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, that's what I want to get clear. When somebody writes a letter that has the title "Warden of KP Dom Foca," that was you, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I'm not competent to discuss this letter --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it your position --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and this proposal. I do not have competence over this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it your position that you're not disputing that this was directed to you and in fact it reached you, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is addressed to the warden of the KP Dom, and it doesn't say to Milorad Krnojelac. In other words, I forwarded this letter, together with the other one, to the Tactical Group, because a part of the KP Dom had been let out to the army. You should understand me. I don't know how to explain it to you. I have no other words to explain to you. And you want me to be brief.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, who delivered this letter to you? It was a guard, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I do not know, but as likely as not, one of the guards who knew well Mr. Pasovic, and he says here that he personally asked Mr. Stanic and Mladjenovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't need to read the letter to us, that's not important what the details are. But you did not have personal contact with Mr. Pasovic, right? This letter was given to you through a guard.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't. No, no, no, no, no. I had no contact. Somebody must have delivered it. For reasons of confidentiality, he gave it to him, and then he gave it to me, and I forwarded it on because it is outside my competence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the intermediary who took the letter from Mr. Pasovic and gave it to you was most likely a guard because those were the people who had contact with the detainees and could deliver these things to you, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is very probable. They could do it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to show you Exhibit D66/2.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is also one of the attachments that you forwarded to the Tactical Group. It's a request by Mr. Demirovic, who was also a detainee, and this request was not addressed to anyone in particular, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sadik Demirovic. I don't know how the letter reached me, but if it did reach me, then it was without doubt sent on to the Tactical Group for consideration because it did not stay in my drawer, that is for certain. It was forwarded, like all the other documents. Any document that reached me was forwarded to the Tactical Group. That is the addressee. And this one, and I can't see here -- yeah, right. I don't see that this was addressed to anyone, but then it must have been forwarded to the Tactical Group, too, because there is now the name of the addressee.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that you forwarded this on to the Tactical Group, but it is a fact, isn't it, that this request ended up in your hands so that you could forward it on, right? It came to you.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But no sooner did it come to me than it was forwarded on, and it was forwarded on because I did that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was brought to you, again, most likely through a guard who got the letter from Mr. Demirovic and delivered it to you, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so, yes. Highly likely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or perhaps one of the administrative clerks, if he knew him, perhaps, and then gave it to some administrative worker. But in one way or the other, that is how it came to me. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in other words, through somebody who was working in the KP Dom at that time, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We don't need this document any more. Mr. Krnojelac, in order to forward the first document to the Crisis Staff and then also to forward the second set of documents to the Foca Tactical Group, you had to have their addresses, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A document -- when I received a document, I would write with a pencil the reference number, then send it on to the registration office, and then that office would forward it on to the addressee.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "registration office," what exactly do you mean? Was there an office within the KP Dom that took care of outgoing mail?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A person responsible for mail, and their room in which that person works, that is what I called it. And that person responsible for the mail would forward that mail to the addressee.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The person responsible for the mail leaving KP Dom was responsible for all the mail leaving KP Dom, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if it had to do with the economic unit, then yes. If it was something else or, rather, somebody else, then he was not responsible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying that that mail person was not responsible for any military mail?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military mail never came to the economic unit except that request for the lease of KP Dom, but it was addressed to the KP Dom, the economic unit; that is, the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying that the mail person that you're talking to -- I'm sorry, that the mail person that you refer to did not handle any military mail at all, that it was one person who was only working for the Drina Economic Unit with regard to mail? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The KP Dom belonged to the Ministry of Justice, and it did not account to anyone else but the Ministry of Justice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you -- the letters that we just looked at and you had addressed to the Foca Tactical Group and the Crisis Staff did not have any addresses on it, so it's fair to say that the person in the mail room knew where these letters would be sent, right? That person knew the address?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they would, surely. Or perhaps there was the address on the envelope, on the envelope.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which envelope?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it would be put in an envelope with the same address as on the document, if you understand what I mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You -- in the letters that we have just read, there is no street address, it simply says, for example, "Crisis Staff." Was that sufficient to get the letter delivered?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know -- I see no reason why not. Why wouldn't it be so, if it is a written document?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there was somebody who could deliver this to the Crisis Staff and to the Foca Tactical Group, if that was the address written on the envelope?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you received these requests from the three detainees, they weren't in sealed envelopes, right? You read them?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember reading them. As soon as I would see the addressee, I could already then say whether one could see it from the subject. I don't remember reading them. There was no need for me to read them. As soon as you see a request for release, that is the subject, you know what else it says, so why should I read it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you read them enough to know that they were in fact requests for release, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, in the first line, the subject, it says reference, it says what it's about, so there is no need to read the text. And perhaps that was even in the envelope and I never opened it. Perhaps it said on the envelope, and you send it together with the envelope. Perhaps that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm terribly sorry, Mr. Krnojelac, you're talking now about envelopes. The three letters that you forwarded on which were requests for release were not in sealed envelopes, were they? You read the letters, maybe not thoroughly, but they were open to you so you knew what they were about, right? This would be -- go on.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you perhaps, maybe, perhaps they already were in their envelopes and perhaps it said on the envelope "to the Crisis Staff" or "to the warden of the KP Dom," and then came the letter. Perhaps it need not be, but if you read the addressee, then there is no need to read the contents of the letter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to have to show you Exhibit 66 and 67 again. First let's start with 67.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: This is D66 and 67?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Krnojelac, in this letter, which you signed, it specifically says, "Please find enclosed the request of detainee Enes Zekovic for release from detention." So you knew exactly what it was about. It was not in any sort of envelope that just had "Crisis Staff" on it, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but please, couldn't it be possible that it said on the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. envelope "to the Crisis Staff of the Serb Municipality," and then Milorad writes on a paper in his hand, "Forward it," and then this is attached to the envelope and sent on. That was a possibility. And then it is merely sent on to the person indicated on the addressee or on the case itself, on the subject itself, unless it was in an envelope. But if it was in an envelope, then I surely did not open the envelope to read it but I'd look to see who it was intended for and then I would forward it to the addressee. I don't know why you can't understand that, or is it that I'm explaining it badly?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I certainly understand that you wish the court to believe that this was a possibility. I understand that much. But let me ask you this: A detainee, like a prisoner, was certainly not allowed to send mail out freely without it being inspected for content, right? That is regular, standard procedure for any sort of detention centre or prison.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know if it went through censorship or inspection. I'm not aware of that, because it was the military part and I do not know what kind of procedure they applied.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You want the court to believe that a sealed envelope came to you that was addressed to the Crisis Staff, that you didn't open it but merely sent it on, and yet you wrote a letter to the Crisis Staff telling them that you were sending it on? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am putting it to you and saying under full responsibility that if it was sealed, then I did not open it, nor did I inspect it, nor did I have any authority to do it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to show you now D66. Mr. Krnojelac, are you telling us that these requests for release that you forwarded on to the Foca Tactical Group also arrived to you in sealed envelopes?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it said on it "to the Tactical Group," and it was sealed, then I didn't open it. On the envelope. If it was in the envelope, or if it said "to the warden of the KP Dom," as it says above this request, then I did open it because I didn't know what it was about. But then, if I saw that it was to the warden but requesting the release from prison, then I would seal this envelope and forward the document to the Tactical Group because their warden was in the Tactical Group in that case. But depends on what it said on the envelope. If it said "to the warden of the KP Dom," then I would open it, because it could be something personal or whatever. But as soon as I opened the document and see that it has to do with a release and know I can do nothing about it, then I send it on to the person authorised to deal with these matters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the course of doing that, you took the trouble of writing a note that you signed, saying that you were forwarding these requests, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's my signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We don't need these documents any more.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I forwarded it on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Regarding Mr. Enes Zekovic, isn't it true that sometime after the 19th of April 1992, you received a call from your friend Zarko Vukovic, forwarding a request orally from Mr. Zekovic's relative to have him released? Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I put it to you that Mr. Vukovic never did that, because Mr. Vukovic knew only too well that I had nothing to do with those people as regards their release and their departure and their -- their release from prison. And I do not even know Mr. Enes Zekovic, I mean, if I met him in the street and said, "Well, this is Enes Zekovic." All I heard was that he was employed in the municipal hall of Foca, but what his job was there, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it true that you told Zarko Vukovic that you couldn't guarantee that Enes Zekovic would be released but that he wouldn't be beaten?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not true, because Zarko Vukovic did not ask me that or say that because he knew it himself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Zekovic, Enes Zekovic, was released in about June 1992; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea when he was released, nor do I know when he was released.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Krnojelac, you've stated that when you came to the KP Dom that there was a great deal of damage, and you've told us that this was inflicted by the Muslims when they were in the KP Dom. Isn't it true that the -- there were also other Serb military forces in the KP Dom before you arrived?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before I arrived there was this Uzice group, as I've already said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They arrived before me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't actually know whether members of the Uzice group, who were Serbs, inflicted damage on the KP Dom, do you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They said that they found it in the state that I found it in, and that is what was recorded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you believed them. You took their word for it, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the commission itself wrote this document, that it had been destroyed, probably because there was also civilian population accommodated there. That is what I heard from others, that there was civilian population was accommodated there during the operations in Foca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question to you, sir, is you don't actually know for a fact that the damage that you found at KP Dom when you arrived was inflicted by the Muslims rather than by the Serbs, do you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I know is that my commission noted that, and I trusted that commission which drew up the record of the situation of the state that the KP Dom was in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The commission wasn't in existence before the group from Uzice came to the KP Dom, right? The damage they assessed was after that group had already arrived.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the commission couldn't come during the military operations. They came afterwards, naturally. And the commission then noted that those were the effects, because the unit from Uzice could not have papers, regs. I don't think they would be strewing things about and breaking down tables. Of course, it is possible, one could not exclude it, but I did not see it and I cannot say that it was something else. All I saw -- all I did was agree with them that damage had been inflicted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, some of the damage you found at the KP Dom was inflicted by shells dropped onto the KP Dom, right? Not just from people within it.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the record also says somewhere that, yes, that there was this two shells and fragments of shells and bullets. The damage was caused by the combat operations, a large part of that. Because broken glass and broken doors, well, this is physical destruction, and the rest, logically the consequence -- the aftermath of fighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your commission could not determine who dropped those shells on KP Dom, could it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was fighting. Who fired them?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I neither saw nor knew nor took part in the fighting to know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Part of the job of the guards at the KP Dom was to make sure that people didn't come in and do damage to the property, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I know, that is why it is called the internal and external security. And I suppose the superior had told them what they were to do and how to act in those jobs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And especially the external security, they would have been important to the functioning of your job in securing the safety of the property, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All these outside facilities were locked up, and even if there were not a man there responsible for it, but an incidental passerby could be logically expected to protect it so it doesn't get destroyed any further. So it must have been within that context that they did it because as soon as you have a man there, then another man won't dare come and break the door as soon as he sees a guard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If a guard of external security was somehow not doing his job Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. correctly and allowed somebody to come in who destroyed the property of the KP Dom, you would have had a complaint against that guard, right, for allowing the destruction of property?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps I would have complained about him, but I wouldn't have the right to punish him or anything because I had not appointed him to that position. Then I would have to appoint a different guard who would only guard that gate, that entrance. But since that did not happen, no other guards were put there except for the security that was there at the external part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To whom would you have complained about such a guard?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I could not complain to anyone, nor could I punish him. Then I would somehow have to provide a person from among the work obligations to stand guard there. But fortunately, I didn't have to think about that. But it could have happened, but it didn't happen. Not that I know of, that somebody broke through a door or -- except that once a window was broken in the restaurant and a few wine bottles and juices were stolen, but that was an outside job.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say the restaurant, which restaurant do you mean; the one outside the KP Dom or the one inside?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Outside the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the right bank of the Drina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to clear up something that's on the transcript. The transcript reflects that at first when you were asked about what you would do, you said that, "Perhaps I would have complained about the guard, but I wouldn't have the right to punish him." And then later on you say no, you could not complain to anyone. Could you complain to anyone if a guard permitted someone to come and destroy property? That was within your jurisdiction, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether there would be any use from that or not, but I know that I naturally could send a letter of that kind to the Tactical Group or, rather, the military command saying that that kind of thing was happening. Or I would inform the police station and then let them use their own know-how as to what should be done and against whom proceedings should be initiated, that's what I meant. Because I would like it to be obvious that I had taken measures in order to stop the damage of property, and then, according to law, somebody else would investigate why such a person did such a thing or whether this person was attacked by someone else and he had no choice, things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also stated - I just want to get this clarified - "I would somehow have to provide a person from among the work obligation to stand guard there, but fortunately I didn't have to think about that." Do you mean that you had the authority to appoint somebody to stand guard specifically to guard property?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, did I? For example, the kiosk where salespeople were selling, it was their duty to come a few times during the night to see whether the kiosk had been looted. And then in the morning if he would come and if he would see that the kiosk had been looted, then he'd have to report to the police station, and then an inventory would be made of all the things that went missing, and then the police would take action. They would look for the thief, and now whether they would find him or not, that is debatable, like many other things, even in peacetime, let alone in wartime.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you're talking about kiosks in Foca where products from the KP Dom were being sold, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only the KP Dom; where products that were obtained through barter were -- and also furniture, for things that you would find. So various goods were sold in these kiosks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So regarding security, then, the same people who were guarding the KP Dom compound were there to guard the people as well as the property, right? There was no --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never told them to guard property, but since these are workers of the KP Dom, they probably consider this to be their own, because I never consider myself a person who would stay there for long as warden. It was quite obvious. A warden had to have a university education, and they were aware of the fact that I would be leaving sooner rather than later. And it was theirs because they had left a large part of their lives there, their careers, so it was only logical for them to safeguard that property.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was no separate guard division or police security service that was guarding only the property, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the Drina Economic Unit also did not have its own security force, did it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only at the farm, at the farm over there. It had to over there because the farm is a separate part, and it is semi-open, if you can put it that way. It's that type of a prison, because they had to have security there not only because of the detained persons, but also so that someone from the outside would not come to steal a cow, a pig, whatever could be stolen, that is, so that is where this special security was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But even those special security people were within the administration of the main security at KP Dom, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. These were separate people who were appointed for work obligation at the Brioni farm, except if someone in the meantime, due to certain justified reasons, would be transferred from the security of the KP Dom to the farm, and then that person would not have to return for -- to work for the security of the KP Dom. I know about that. I know about one particular case of a man's son getting killed in the war, and he even had a nervous breakdown and all that, and then he was transferred to the farm after that, when he got back from sick leave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us, sir, that Mitar Rasevic was in charge of the guards at the KP Dom. Who was in charge of the guards at the farm?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Throughout that work, it was Mr. Novica Mojovic who was in charge of them at the farm and he appointed some of these senior guards, so they took turns. It was important for shifts to be determined. Milorad would be standing guard here today at such and such a date, and then, instead of him, such and such a person would be standing guard the other day. Just in order to rotate it. It wasn't really a problem. This is a pretty small area anyway. This is hilly, mountainous terrain. It's small. So there was no special person who was appointed commander except if he would, say, make up the shifts and see who will be on the security details, but people who worked at the farm knew.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When Muslim detainees came from the KP Dom compound to work on the farm, they were guarded by the guards at the farm, right, during the time that they were there?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether it was always that way, but I assume that they guarded them, but sometimes perhaps others came as well. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So sometimes guards from the KP Dom did come to the farm, right? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when the Muslim detainees worked on the farm, they were side by side with the Serb convicted prisoners working on the farm, right? They worked together?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not say that they worked side by side because there was no need for them to work side by side. If these detained persons from the KP Dom would happen to come, then they would do something at a particular place, whereas these other people did their everyday jobs that they were supposed to do, so they did not have to be working side by side ever; I mean together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When there were Muslim detainees and Serb convicted prisoners working at the farm at the same time, did they share the same security service, the same people guarding both groups?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know all the details about this because I didn't go there. Late Novica Mojovic knew about it, and the rest of the company who were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were times when the Serb convicted prisoners were working in the KP Dom compound at the same time as the Muslim detainees, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the compound, Muslim detainees? They didn't work there except in the factory, in the compound, except the factory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is what I mean. When they worked in the factory and the metalwork shop, there were both Serb prisoners and Muslim detainees at the same time, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there was a special one, I wouldn't know, but there was some -- somebody with some special skills, they would probably work together, but I am not aware, I -- I don't know it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But when the furniture factory is running, when people are working there - and you've told us that there were Muslim detainees as well as Serb prisoners working in the factory - they had the same security service, right? It wasn't different guards assigned only for the Muslim detainees and then another set of guards assigned only for the Serb prisoners. It was all the same when they were working in the factory; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me when I say that I do not know if there were such cases when Serb and Muslims worked at one and the same time, because these three or four, depends, they mostly dealt with Mr. Lazar Divljan as regards the stocks and these things, so that I am not aware if they worked in the furniture factory. Perhaps it did happen later on, but I am not aware that they worked, except they helped Lazar with the storeroom, with the loading, unloading, packing and that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "these three or four," are you referring to Serbs or Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about persons serving their time. I'm talking about persons serving their time. But if you're -- since you're asking me about Serbs, they who had committed some petty offences, I don't know about this, whether they mingled or not. That's what the security -- the guards know and their chief.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The people serving their terms, then, were the ones that you refer to as working with the warehouse person, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those who had been convicted and were serving their terms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when they were working with the warehouse person, they were not being guarded, were they?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there is no need to guard them. Those were people who had been vetted. There was no need to guard them, because they were aware -- had they wanted to, as soon as the thing earlier happened - and you heard it from statements - as soon as the gate was opened, had they wanted to, they would have fled the KP Dom. So they were not people who wanted to escape anywhere because they had the opportunity to escape and not serve their sentences any longer, as soon as the penitentiary was open.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you this, then, since you've told us that you were in charge of these people doing -- serving their sentences: Based on what you told us, you considered them a very low security risk, right? You didn't consider it necessary to guard them very tightly against escape?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were kept separately in the building. So from the building, he goes to the warehouse, does what he has to do, and goes back to the building. As far as I can understand, they were in that part in the building facing the furniture factory, on an upper floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Krnojelac, I'm not asking you just about the few people working with the warehouse worker, but the 25 or so convicted persons serving their sentence that you've told the court you were in charge of; you didn't consider any of them a high security risk, did you, and you treated them accordingly, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, but not all these people were in the KP Dom. They were at the Brioni farm, and Mr. Novica Mojovic was responsible for them, and he had assumed that responsibility. And he said he'd take care of them and employ them because he needed them most at the -- on the farm, because they had to do all those jobs that had to be done on the farm, and that is why I was not all that concerned about them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry if I misunderstood you, so let me get this cleared up. Mr. Mojovic was basically in charge of the farm so there was no need for you to go there very often and oversee what was happening there, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was responsible, but he left quite often for various reasons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did go there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, whenever I asked you questions about the farm, you've told us that Mr. Mojovic was in charge, and so my question to you was: You didn't have very much to do with the farm. It was Mr. Mojovic who was dealing with the everyday running of it. You were simply his superior, right? But the details --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went there quite often. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you went there that often, you seem not to know a great deal about the issues I'm asking you about. I've asked you about the guards, and you've told us that you were not there that often. Now you're telling us that you were there very often.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if I went to see if the production was progressing, if there was any shortage of food, if some other food had to be obtained, then we didn't talk about guards, and there was no need to, because he was the top one there. And to be quite honest, it would happen at times, well, there's nothing to do here, so let's go and see what about things there, whether there is a need to go and purchase something for them or just have a cup of coffee over there, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there were -- most of the convicted people serving their sentences were housed at the farm, right? The overwhelming majority actually were housed at the farm rather than the KP Dom complex?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because there were also rooms where they could be -- where they could put up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the question that I started this discussion with was regarding those people and whether you felt that they were a security risk. You didn't think that they were a high risk of fleeing, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The risk, there was no risk, because there wasn't a single attempt, so that one did not have to think and guard against their trying to escape or not trying to escape.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you about your relationship with Mr. Mojovic. You were his superior, right, in the hierarchy?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, according to red tape.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which means that if something happened, if he did something, that you would be responsible to -- for that as his superior, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if there was something going on at the farm, you made sure to be informed about it, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right, that I should be informed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it wasn't the kind of situation where, if you didn't see it, you could just say, "Well, I didn't see it so I'm not responsible for that," right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't put it that way, but if it -- if something happened, then somebody must be responsible. I mean, whenever something is done, somebody must be responsible for it. And in that case, he would be the first one to account for it, and then I wouldn't do anything about it unless I wrote a paper to the ministry because if something like that happened, then I would have to write to the ministry to know who did something and what he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you found out that somebody at the farm did something wrong, you would have to find out about it and, if you could, punish that person, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no rules of the procedure to punish anyone. I merely find out, investigate, and if an offence had been committed or if something that I didn't know what to do with it, then I would notify the ministry in writing as to what had been done, what had been found out, and they would, I suppose, issue me with the guidelines as to what to do and how to resolve it. Whether I should be dismissed or the one who did that, they would decide as to what would need to be done next. Because I came from teaching, I couldn't really be familiar with all those mechanisms and laws and how these things were resolved. That is how I would have acted had something like that happened, but it didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the procedures that you've outlined for us now were known to you at that time, right, in case something did happen?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, had something happened, that is how I would have done, as I have just told you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you found out that one of the persons serving their term at the farm had been beaten up by one of the staff members, you would have to investigate that, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to initiate the investigation and notify the ministry of such an incident, and then they would tell me what I should do next, or perhaps they would take over the case. But I would have to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Krnojelac, I'd like to ask you about your house, and we've heard a lot of testimony about the workers who came to fix your house. You've told us that you made the request to the municipality and that after that, without your making any arrangements for the details, materials arrived for your house, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, what time are you referring to? When is it they made that -- applied for it? What time, what period of time do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking about the time frame in late 1992 that you made -- you've told us you made a request for your house to be repaired about a month or two before the end of that year, right? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, I did not say -- give me that document and that proof that I had made that request. I went to the municipal hall of Foca and found Mr. Radovic who was responsible, who was in charge of refugees and those whose houses had burnt down. And orally I asked him to give me something, whether a tent, a tarpaulin, or perhaps some plastic sheets to protect the surface of the building, which was roofless, to protect it against further ruin. I didn't submit any request for repair. Don't -- unless you have a document to this effect, then don't accuse me of making such a request. It was an oral application to protect it from further ruin because I wanted to return to that house, if luck would serve me --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, sir --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KRNOJELAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- with my family, and I wanted to protect it against further ruin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, no one accused you or said anything about making a written request. The question was whether you've made any sort of a request, and you've now told us that it was an oral request.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And I think it's time for lunch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, we'll adjourn now. We'll resume at 2.30 when we will take Ms. Najman's evidence. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.00 22 23 24 25

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, the Trial Chamber has had a look at this report that was prepared by Ms. Najman. It consists of a history that she has taken and the results of a number of tests and then her conclusions drawn on those. Would it not save an immense amount of time if you just tendered the report and allowed her to add anything or you took her through the matters arising out of the Prosecution witness's report you want to, rather than letting her read it out?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I agree, it does sound sensible, but I would have to ask Mr. Vasic because he took care of this subject as I was responsible for the examination of the accused, so if -- with your leave, Mr. Vasic will take over from me now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Certainly. We don't want in any way to limit what you elicit from Ms. Najman, but it seems to me this is not like the statement of a witness telling us what happened many years ago. This is the history she took, which she obviously must have taken notes at the time, it's the report of the tests she applied and her conclusions, and you can ask her to expand upon them or deal with them in any way. It's interesting to listen to a witness giving evidence, but nevertheless, it will save an immense amount of time if we just put the report in and you proceed from there. Do you have any problem with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, none, Your Honour, thank you. The Defence will tender the report marked ID D145 and 145A, and we shall only ask questions regarding some details which it seems to us need further clarification and I do believe that your suggestion is a very good one. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I do have to ask the Prosecution about it yet. Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, it seems to be the simplest way of dealing with it, don't you think?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Very well. Then they will be Exhibits D145 and D145A and you can assume we have read them, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Najman, would you mind standing while we have you make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Please sit down. Examined by Mr. Vasic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Madam. Will you please give us your name.

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: Ana Najman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give us the date of your birth and the place.

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: 25th March, 1951, Subotica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have received your expert opinion, so could you please tell us, only briefly, what experience do you have?

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: I graduated from the faculty of philosophy, the clinical stream, and I underwent specialisation, three-year long, at the faculty of medicine in Belgrade. And then forensic psychology, family psychology, group psychology were further subspecialisations. And from 1976 onward, that is for about 25 years, is the seniority I have behind me. I worked in a school, then at a social work centre, then in the city hospital for about ten years where I acquired very important forensic experience. And now I work at the clinical psychiatry at the Dragisa Misevic Clinical Medical Centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us if you have any publications? Have you published anything?

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: Yes. At -- the Yugoslav Forensic Society holds various meetings, and I always submitted reports, either based on my practical experience or in theoretical works. I also attended various psychologists meetings in Serbia and Yugoslavia covering different fields, both theoretical and clinical experience in group psychology and various other related matters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As an expert witness, have you already testified in other cases?

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: Yes. I am the expert for Yugoslavia since 1996 -- 1986, and now I testified here in Mr. Dokmanovic's case, Radic's case, Krnojelac's case, and I'm currently involved in the Dosen case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us, on the basis of Mr. Krnojelac's case history, what was -- how was Mr. Krnojelac motivated by his parents when he was still a child as to his future career?

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: The principal guidelines given him by his parents, who were rather poor, were to encourage him to receive education, to seek advancement, and try to leave that poor environment. His mother was particularly active in this regard, and his emotional relationship with his mother was also very good.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, how long did it take him to become a teacher of mathematics?

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: Well, he first completed elementary education, then enrolled in secondary school, then moved over to the teachers college, and after that, he also came out of the higher school for mathematics and physics teachers in Sarajevo. Officially, he came out of the higher school for the teachers of mathematics and physics in 1970, that is, when he was 30. Meanwhile, he also worked so that his education was, in a way, specific. It wasn't a conventional kind of education and there was no continuity; that is, first you finish all your schools and then find a job. He finished a part of this education, started to work, and then went back to further education.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you deduce from the case history if Milorad Krnojelac has any -- has ever had any conflict with the environment?

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: According to him, that is, on the basis of his case history, we learned that he has never been punished, that he has never had any conflict, that he never even got into a fight. This was the information that I received.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Will you just make a short break -- wait for a little after you hear my question so as to give time for the interpreters to fully interpret both my question and your answer. Thank you. And did you find out when you established the case history what happened to the family and the house of Milorad Krnojelac in 1992, and how did he react to it psychologically?

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: The case history showed that on the 15th of April that year, his house burnt down. He had left it a day before that, hastily getting ready and leaving with the rest of his family to his brother's who lived in another village. He mentioned that the house is mostly surrounded by Muslim people, and he did not think that he should leave the house because he did not see the situation leading to anything, so that he left the house and watched from a hill -- watched his house burning from a hill. That was around the 16th of April 1992, and he was visibly shattered. He and his family all cried. And of course, this was a very stressful event, not only for him. It is stressful in general. And it was very hard for him to accept that, to live with it and accept it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the same hold true of the situation when his two sons were wounded, one of whom lost both his legs and the other one who had had injuries and lost a part of his leg?

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: Of course, if we -- by analogy, by psychologic analogy, of course it is also highly -- high stress. So this incident, the loss of a house, the loss of the home, not house as a building, but of a home, the wounding of the sons, these are very -- very grave things. Illnesses, tragedies, these are highly stressful events, and they're evaluated as events of high stress.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how does psychology define stress?

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: Stress is a general reaction of the body. It is a set of non-specific reactions of the body to any request for adjustment to some changed conditions in the environment. It is closely related to emotional experience, and the higher the stress, the stronger the emotions. In the international classification of diseases, DSM-III-R and in the latest IC-III-10, the types of these I call social stress factors are classified, and it says that it includes marital; family; psychosocial; legal, meaning arrest, investigation, trial, et cetera; then stress caused by some somatic diseases; injuries; and some either psychosocial stresses such as war, persecution, painful, traumatic events in war and armed conflicts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, madam. In your expertise on page 5, you said that Mr. Krnojelac does not easily -- has difficulty understanding instructions given him when he's invited to do the test. What instructions do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: When tests are given to the examinees, there is a general rule abided by most psychologists. It's a general rule, and identical for all the examinees. It does not presume any additional explanations or any additional assistance because the rule has been formulated in a manner in which every examinee can understand it. Of course, from the case history of that person, we learn what is the level of education of the examinee, and the tests are then suited to that. When I mentioned these instructions, I meant in the first place that the examinee requested additional explanations and he did not immediately and straight away understand what he was being asked to do, which is not a common phenomenon and below our psychological expectations of someone who is -- who teaches mathematics, who teaches children, and who would, under normal circumstances, always understand such a thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. On the same page, you also say that you interrupted that test at a moment because the examinee did not feel well. Could you describe to us what Mr. Krnojelac looked like at the moment when you said that.

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: Mr. Krnojelac exerted himself to apply the instructions he had received to the test, but he had difficulty with that, and then he started to feel insecure. He sweated, he was upset, very pale at some point, and said that he was feeling weak. I think we offered some water with sugar to him, and he appeared as a person who was emotionally very disturbed and in a specific state. I wouldn't call -- I wouldn't attach to it any specific diagnostic name, but from the point of view of his behaviour and what he looked like, that is how I would describe it. And then I decided to interrupt the test and do it the next day. After that, he pulled his wits about and we did something else, and when we did that, he did not show the symptoms so that we went back to this task the next day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you briefly analyse Mr. Krnojelac's intellectual abilities.

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: Well, as I have already said, the result -- the results of that test were not brilliant. He was at the level of a poorer average during that test. It is a test intending -- intended to examine the logical reasoning, and we call it culture-free test because it has nothing to do with one's level of education and other cultural factors. Another test that I gave him was a test to measure general abilities, and there, the result was even lower. Of course, I say, because when solving these tests, the examinees - not Mr. Krnojelac alone but any examinee - has a momentary feedback about whether he has resolved it well or not. That is, he already has an impression of what he is relatively good at and how good he is at something. The more difficult he found to solve the tasks and the more trouble he had with solving them, he -- the more he became insecure, the more he became upset, and it resulted in a heightened anxiety, which then affected, in its turn, the result, and so the result was below what we expected of a teacher of mathematics. So that I can say that what was -- what -- the manifestations of his intellectual abilities, as we would call it in psychology, did not go above the lower average. And that, of course, is different from the level of the primary intellectual potential. Perhaps I should clarify it a little because, in this finding, I use the -- these notions, the active level of the intellectual functioning and the primary intellectual potential. The primary intellectual potential is something that one is possessed of. That is, I won't say that he is born with it, but that is one's ability that one develops over time. And the active potential can be disrupted in different situations by different factors. One of them is this one that I've told you about, not to repeat myself, that is insecurity, anxiety and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You have explained to us the level of Mr. Krnojelac's intellectual ability. Could you then tell us, explain to us or define to us his way of thinking?

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: Of course, on the level of the intellectual potential and abilities also presumes the level of thinking. Roughly speaking, we could Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. divide it into the concrete and the abstract level. I can say that the level of abstract thinking is practically absent or barely present. It is very difficult to register it. But the concrete level of thinking prevailed, and this was particularly obvious during Raven's test which observes the ability to discriminate between the important and unimportant, understanding of certain global features, and it showed a certain mental rigidity and, up to a point, marked psycho-motor slowness, torpidity. This perhaps could be due, as I have already said, to the examinee's behaviour under the circumstances and the personality factors which came into play, and the second part should be attributed to a somehow lower intellectual capacity in general.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In your finding when you described Mr. Krnojelac's personality, you used terms such as somatisation, hypersensitivity, combined with characteristics of passive structures of a personality, and you said that these were the principal characteristics of this category of examinees. Could you tell us, on the basis of what did you draw such conclusions?

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: Outside from the psychological interview on the basis of which we establish a diagnosis of patients and therefore an evaluation of the personality, also applied some personality tests, and I used the projective test and the MMPI test. The MMPI test or a personality inventory, which describes the current profile of the examinee's personality, were predominated by hypochondriac tendencies and very highly on the scale, then suppression and denial and anxiety. And all this was accompanied by a mild subdepression symptoms, I would say, rather than depression symptoms. In psychology, such a personality profile is usually described with these words that I used them, that is, hypersensitivity, and a passivity is something that prevails in his personality structure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me, in view of the tests that you applied, that you have just told us about, could you also point out to us some other characteristics which might be relevant with reference to Mr. Krnojelac's personality?

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: Of course. The examinee appeared as a very sociable, extrovert personality, a very cooperative one, ready to draw attention in one way or the other, but this is something that had also to do with the work with the tests and his behaviour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned the characteristics Mr. Krnojelac showed during the tests. Can you tell me if during the tests, if in these tests, the examinee perhaps could present himself in a more desirable light than is actually the case?

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: Of course, these tests, and by this I mean MMPI especially and Pluchick's test and Elizur's questionnaire, and they all have scale which is called a life scale in MMPI and Pluchick, and these are scales used to measure the manner in which the examinee presents. Not the lack of -- not the truthfulness but the way in which he understands the test, the way in which he solves it, and thus in which he gives manifestation of some of his traits. The L scale, the so-called lie scale, and these scales were at a level which enabled us to accept the results and thereby approve the validity of the test results, which means that at the moment, that while the examinee saw these tests, the examinee did not try to present himself in a more desirable, in a more socially-acceptable light. When these scales are very high, perhaps I should mention this, we do not think that the examinee is lying in the specific meaning of this word, but that he merely tries to conceal some of his traits that he deems not to be particularly favourable or that are unfavourable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But this was not the case at that time of Mr. Krnojelac's examination?

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: That is quite right. I did point that out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, the tests that you mentioned, did Mr. Krnojelac -- is perhaps any aggressiveness a marked trait of Mr. Krnojelac or, perhaps, lack of control? Is he a very impulsive man?

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: No, and I believe I did refer to this somewhere in my finding. Neither the impulsiveness or aggressiveness were marked, either in the PIE or Pluchick the Rorschach, which is the relevant scale for subconscious mechanisms. The profile -- had it not been so, the profile we got would be somewhat different because in that case, the scales of psychosomatic deviations or abnormality would be higher. On the MMPI, for instance, that was something that would have been manifest, obvious, straight away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Najman. You summed up the intellectual capacities of Milorad Krnojelac, and taking into account the level of his intellectual ability and his occasional anxiety and fits of psychological weakness, how did he behave while he was working in the school as a teacher?

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: You see, I can point out that I myself have some modest experience of work in the school environment. I can say that any teacher gets certain curriculum and prepares for it. These preparations is something that they have always ready, and it serves as a basis for their lectures and also serves the basis for an assessment to see whether the, the curriculum was duly covered. In other words, what I'm saying is that this is a well-known situation, and Mr. Krnojelac was part -- well aware of this system, familiar with it. In other words, he was able to prepare, and this gives him self-assurance, this gives him confidence, and this was probably transferred to his students. The situation of his examination, if I can call it that, in other words, measurements of his own intellectual capabilities, is, and this is something that has come on to every person, it is something that is frustrating for everyone to a lesser or greater degree. It is a situation that really deviates from the standard or standarised or strictly controlled situation such as we have in school when he is preparing for a lecture, for instance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you then tell us, please, taking all this into account, how did Mr. Krnojelac behave in situations that were completely new and unknown to him?

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: Of course, new situations mobilised some other mechanisms in him such as insecurity, lack of self-confidence, passivity, and that produced an increased amount of anxiety, his willingness to put off or delay such situations or to be ambivalent, as the technical term would say, and if in situations when he is not fully able to control the situation, he gets out of it and asks -- and directs people or himself to not participate in it any longer. These are also characteristics of a -- of the passive personality, which is what I pointed out in my finding. This is one of those characteristics. And it also manifested in Mr. Krnojelac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So what was the behaviour of Mr. Krnojelac in the situation of receiving orders?

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: In a situation of receiving orders, of course, again, the characteristic of the passive personality structure reappears, and it is something that is characteristic of him. He upsets it in a passive way. He does not find the strength to resist them. In his own way, he is obedient to the authority that has given him such orders but taking to -- taking into account the level of his intellectual operating and his passive personality, he does not undertake a deep and wide analysis of the possible consequences of such an order. If we go back to what I have previously said about the characteristics of his way of thinking, I think that this clarifies that point now, because he does not demonstrate such curiosity, a spirit of examination and analysis, because he does not show such a primary characteristic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Taking that into account, what is his attitude towards work in situations like this?

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: In regard to the work-type situations, Mr. Krnojelac behaves in a hyperactive way, if we can put it that way. He is very engaged, he is industrious, and it is -- he seems to be compelled by it, by some kind of inner mechanism of his. We can point to the defence mechanisms that guided his behaviour, which imply different ways in which sound parts of personality defend themselves in situations when they are threatened either from inside or outside and the threat is such that it threatens the very balance or homeostasis of personality. On the basis of tests which I applied to Mr. Krnojelac - and this is what I pointed out - these were the dominant mechanisms. It was suppression and denial. It is a primary mechanism for this type of personality, which is demonstrated in situations when he cannot control or rule over such situations, psychologically speaking. They are not a conscious part of personality. They are dictated by unconscious impulses, and it's not a rational type of defence, that is the suppression or isolation of affects or denial. It is an unconscious mechanism which is triggered off when the sound part of personality feels that their strength is disappearing and when they cannot control situations which come either from within or without. It can be a traumatic event, something that can be encountered in difficult or catastrophic situations. It would have to do with death or pain and situations like that. So this type of personality resorts to this in order to retain some kind of sanity in their personality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, madam. You told us how Mr. Krnojelac behaved in new circumstances, in situations that -- in which he was not used, and in situations where he was receiving orders. Can you now turn to the characteristics of his personality in situations when he is brought into a situation to do something which he had never done before and taking into account that was a wartime situation on top of that?

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: You see, I believe that in points 3 and 4 of the summary addresses this issue, and I can repeat now that the level of functioning of personality is something that is characteristic for a person throughout their lives. It is a style of behaviour. It is a type of behaviour that stretches for the length of their lives. Of course, stress situations coming from within or without, wartime, disasters, it is something that is -- anything that is above normal and usual only exacerbates what I have just mentioned, in terms of the functioning of personality. That would mean that such a person in these situations is even more anxious, even more insecure, and attempts to follow orders and reach decisions that are expected of it, because there is a trait of obedience and conformity, which I think I may not have mentioned but it is in the finding, and a desire to please some of the authorities. But also he is not able to process all this emotionally, and at the moment when the level of suffering reaches a point where the person is not able to emotionally or cognitively process it, such a person retreats, becomes passive and very frequently just leaves this situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Najman. Can you tell me, madam, did you have an opportunity to look at the finding of Madam Folnegovic and do you have it on you?

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look at that opinion of Madam Folnegovic-Smalc and to tell me whether you agree with this opinion? Does it correspond to what you have found in your own finding?

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
utterances.text: I very carefully read the opinion, and I think that our descriptions and our conclusions, if not identical, are still very, very close. For instance, on page 11 of the opinion, Madam Folnegovic-Smalc said that Mr. Krnojelac, according to two classifications, does not have any mental disturbance and that he had no traces of any organically-based or any other mental disease, with which I agree fully. Also, the tests have -- the way I understood the finding of the psychiatric examination showed, on both the qualitative and quantitative basis, she reached the conclusion that he had no mental disturbance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam Najman, thank you. Can you please tell me, in Madam Folnegovic's opinion it says neurotic and panic traits that you pointed out in your expertise, that she considers them models of behaviour. Are you -- do you agree with that position?

utterances.speaker: ANA NAJMAN
